errorSignature: Regex secret fingerprinting produces false positives on placeholder values; a naive 'leak count' can also be zero because the base64 line-wrap was not stripped
finding: While auditing infra/observability/alertmanager.yml, the pattern hooks\.slack\.com/services/T[A-Z0-9]{6,}/B[A-Z0-9]{6,}/[A-Za-z0-9]{20,} matched the deliberate placeholder T00000000/B00000000/XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, falsely suggesting a real Slack webhook. Blob comparison (git rev-parse d22deb0:<path> vs HEAD:<path>) proved blob 5cd59e72 is identical in the initial commit and current main, i.e. no real webhook was ever committed; the corresponding GitHub secret-scanning alert #1 was resolved as false_positive. Separately, counting tokens via gh api contents --jq .content | base64 -d without first running tr -d '\n' yielded false '0 token' results because the API returns newline-wrapped base64.
verificationMethod: git rev-parse <commit>:<path> blob-id equality across commits, plus full-history scan: git log --all --format=%H | while read c; do git show $c:<path>; done | sort -u
preventionRule: Before treating a fingerprint match as a real secret, (1) always strip the base64 newline wrapping with tr -d '\n' before base64 -d when reading files via the GitHub contents API, and (2) disambiguate placeholders from real secrets by comparing blob ids across commits (git rev-parse <sha>:<path>) or by checking for repeated/sequential filler like 00000000/XXXX. Prefer provider-verified detection (GitHub secret scanning validity checks) over regex alone.
